summary.title: Things I Learned the Hard Way
summary.one_liner: Bryan Cantrill's talk distills lessons from his software career, covering learning on the job, testing, tooling, debugging, technology choices, predictions, trust, and hiring around shared values.
keywords: hard way vs easy way learning
takeaways: Most engineering learning happens on the job, and organizations learn best by teaching what they know and learning from mistakes.
Debugging is better approached by asking informed questions of the system than by forming hypotheses; build tooling when you are debugging.
Treat odd behavior as a signal worth understanding, and for rare non-reproducible bugs, make the system leave more state behind.
Choose technologies deliberately and weigh the values they embody; test early and write your own tests.
Hiring mistakes are costly; articulate shared values and let them guide hiring, since interviews alone are flawed.
summary.summary: This is the text of a talk given by Bryan Cantrill to the Rokt engineering team in November 2023, presented as a set of slide-style bullet points. It moves through themes including learning (the easy way via structured organizational teaching versus the hard way through mistakes), testing, building internal tooling, debugging methodology, handling odd and non-reproducible problems, weighing technology choices by their values, the unreliability of predictions, trust and fear on teams, and hiring around shared values. Cantrill draws on his OS kernel work at Sun Microsystems and closes by pointing to social audio and the Oxide and Friends podcast as ways to share experience.
